hypothesis: Image-specific speech targets and direct acoustic loss are a more appropriate alignment test than further template-prior calibration.
scope: Development feasibility and memorization control, not M2 acceptance
selection: First 24 training rows sorted by ID with distinct scene groups, from existing 239-row training cohort; local vision labels; no heldout labels or reserved fresh access
teacher: One 8-18-word Italian sentence grounded in two visible details per accepted image; no prescribed ending. Genuine frozen Qwen audio, seed42 cap160, both variable text paths replaced by cached continuous vectors.
reader: Existing global image MLP width128, variable prefix length fitted only on selected training rows; frozen visual and Qwen backbones
warm_start: 1600 prefix reconstruction steps, actual resume at800; a memorization diagnostic only
acoustic: 320 steps, actual resume at160, codec0 CE including EOS plus 0.1 residual CE; prefix MSE weight zero; learning rate2e-5
controls: Retain exact teacher WAVs; evaluate warm start and acoustic reader on same first4 accepted training IDs, prior exposed4 development IDs, and null; sampled seed42 cap105
interpretation: Training failure implicates alignment/optimization; training success alone does not establish heldout grounding. Human assessment required for quality. No LoRA before this bounded control is inspected.
alternatives: LoRA on last Talker attention layers if frozen acoustic alignment remains inadequate; image-specific corpus expansion if memorization works; visual token resampling only after global representation insufficiency is demonstrated.
privacy: All image labels, per-image evidence, tensors, checkpoints and generated media local; no paid compute
